transcript.text: The lips can make or break a face.
Here are two simple steps with the highest return to naturally improve them.
Step one is fixing lip posture, which radically transforms the perceived dimensions of your lips.
Half of you are tucking your top lip in without even realizing it, which in turn makes it appear thinner,
and many of you are curling the outer corners of your lips downwards without realizing.
The literature indicates that these changes make the face appear less youthful, less friendly, and less attractive.
What you should practice instead is the habit of a gentle pout and the soft smile as a new resting phase
for a younger, kinder, and more esthetic mouth.
The second step is to not just focus on lip size.
Thin lips can still be very attractive if they are hydrated and have sufficient red pigment.
So one of the oldest tricks is to simply make red- or pink-tinted lip balm a staple of your daily routine.
As a man you might think, 'Oh, let me skip the color,'
but Stephen and McKeegan found red pigment also makes men's lips more attractive too,
and tinted lip balm is not like lipstick.
Realistically, if you pick a mild one, you'll look better and nobody will notice why.
There are dozens of small signals like these that shape how your face is perceived,
and we break down all of them over at Qoves.com.

narrative_arc: Hook: Lips make or break a face.
Step 1: Fix lip posture (avoid tucking and curling down).
Scientific backing: Posture affects perceived youthfulness and friendliness.
Solution 1: Practice a gentle pout and soft smile.
Step 2: Focus on hydration and red pigment, not just size.
Solution 2: Use tinted lip balm (applicable to both men and women).
CTA: Visit Qoves.com for full facial analysis.

what_makes_it_work: High-density visual overlays (face meshes, sliders, and metrics) make the content feel highly scientific and objective.
Using recognizable celebrities keeps the viewer engaged and provides clear, relatable examples.
Actionable, low-effort advice (posture adjustment and lip balm) makes the viewer feel they can easily apply the tips.

animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements scale up with elastic overshoot (PopIn) or slide in from edges (SlideIn).
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements typically fade out or are covered by incoming panels.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts combined with sliding panel transitions.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: Background colors and top-level step indicators remain static.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Highly dynamic with constant micro-animations and staggered arrivals to maintain engagement.

what_we_should_steal: The interactive perception slider (Cursor) to simulate real-time analysis.
The scientific paper stacking effect (TagStack) to build instant authority.
The technical face-mesh overlay (ContourDraw) for a premium, analytical aesthetic.
